title: Cost optimizer card lineage & chronicle — apply/rollback transparency
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a clear, linked UI surface in Console Optimize that shows recommendation card lineage, a compact diff preview, and an auditable apply/rollback chronicle so operators can safely accept caching/batching changes and later trace who changed what and why.
background: Customers want automated batching/caching recommendations but are hesitant to accept automated changes without clear ability to preview diffs, understand risk, and rollback safely. Current Optimize cards surface predictions but lack a timeline and immutable audit trail tied to config snapshots and deployment artifacts.
proposal_summary: Introduce a 'Chronicle' panel on each recommendation card that records previews (config diffs), apply events, rollback events, and links to related artifacts (PRs, runbooks, evals). Add a sandboxed preview runner that simulates cost latency delta and shows example traces. Provide a one-click safe rollback that restores previous config snapshot and writes an immutable audit entry.
ux_goals: Make diffs scannable within 3 seconds (compact unified diff view with tokenized highlights)
Expose the exact config keys changed and their prior values
Show economic delta estimates and uncertainty range next to diffs
Permit reversible applies with automatic snapshotting and a labeled rollback button
Surface who approved/applied, timestamp, and linked PR or support ticket
acceptance_criteria: Each recommendation card shows a Chronicle timeline tab with at least: preview snapshot, applied snapshot, and rollback entries
Diff view renders before/after values for batching, cache TTLs, cache key scope, and quantization flags
Apply action creates an immutable snapshot (stored reference id) and writes an audit log entry visible in Audit Trail page
Rollback action restores exact prior snapshot to the runtime config within the SLA window and appends rollback entry
Sandbox preview runner produces a simulated cost and latency delta with 90% CI for selected workload samples
All entries link to one or more artifacts: GitHub PR, Console trace id, or customer ticket
engineering_notes: Backend: introduce snapshot table (snapshot_id, config_blob_ref, created_by, created_at, reason) and immutable audit entries
API: POST /optimize/recommendations/{id}/apply -> returns snapshot_id and audit_id
Rollback should validate runtime compatibility and return a deterministic restore plan
Simulated preview uses historical traces sampled from user's trace bucket (configurable sample size)
qa_checks: Verify diff highlights exactly the keys touched when applying recommendation
Simulate failed apply and ensure rollback does not leave partial state
Confirm audit log entries contain user, timestamp, snapshot_id, and artifact links
Run e2e against Dedicated cluster to validate rollback under pressure (3x traffic)
metrics: Apply acceptance rate (percent of recommendations applied within 14 days)
Mean time to rollback after a failed apply (goal < 30 min)
Reduction in per-token cost for customers who applied caching/batching recommendations
Number of audit lookups per applied recommendation
rollout_plan: Alpha behind feature flag for 10 internal customers
Collect feedback and instrumentation for 2 weeks
Open beta to customers on Optimize tier with opt-in
GA with migration script to snapshot existing manual changes
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Snapshot/rollback may be incompatible with concurrent manual edits — Mitigation: optimistic lock + pre-apply dry-run and conflict modal
Risk: Audit trail grows unbounded — Mitigation: configurable retention and cold storage export
Risk: Customers misinterpret simulated preview — Mitigation: surface CI and sample size prominently
open_questions: Should snapshot blobs be encrypted with customer KMS for Private deployments?
What is the SLA window for safe automatic rollback (30m vs 2h)?
Do we allow automatic scheduled rollbacks or only manual initiations?
